summary: Phase 2 (Custom Playground / Daily Challenge / Race Mode / Sound Effects / +3 bosses) verified end-to-end. Backend 28/28 pytest pass. Frontend playwright tests all pass after appropriate waits for network-bound bot/boss lists.

issues: At xl breakpoint with 10+ nav links the navbar is crowded: 'BOSS FIGHT' wraps to 2 lines and the user pill (LV.3 SENSEI) visually overlaps the EXIT button. Consider hiding avatar/level text on xl and reserving them for full-desktop (2xl), or shortening the label to 'BOSS'.

action_items: Optional: Tidy navbar layout at the xl breakpoint to prevent the 'Boss Fight' wrap and avatar/EXIT visual overlap.
Optional: SessionPayload.mode docstring still says 'lesson | quote | boss' but now also accepts 'daily', 'race', 'custom'. Update the comment for clarity.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: SessionPayload.mode is typed as plain `str` with stale comment. Consider Literal['lesson','quote','boss','daily','race','custom'] for stronger validation, and to reject misspellings that would otherwise silently skip the multiplier (e.g. mode='Daily' would NOT get 2x).

server.py daily endpoint uses date.toordinal() % len(passages) for deterministic per-day passage — good. But /api/race uses the same daily rotation rather than random per-call; consider randomizing per request if 'fresh race' is desired.
evaluate_achievements: streak_3 condition `user.streak+1 >= 3 or user.streak >= 3` is redundant — first clause already implies second.
record_session does not validate `mode` value, so an arbitrary string is accepted into the DB. Add Literal or explicit allow-list.

If future tests re-introduce ordering issues, prefer registering a fresh user per test class instead of sharing `state`.
rca of the issue: Initial UI run reported 8 frontend failures, but they were caused by my test script using wrong register testids (-name/-email vs -name-input/-email-input). After fixing selectors, only 2 transient failures remained (race-bot-genin, boss-card-boss1) and those resolved cleanly with `wait_for_selector` rather than `is_visible` — the cards are rendered after an async API fetch. No production frontend code was at fault.
